headline: Germany Smashes Solar Record With 12 Billion kWh in July
meta_description: Germany hit a historic solar milestone in July 2026, feeding 12 billion kWh into the grid for the first time ever.
summary_short: Germany achieved its first month ever exceeding 12 billion kWh of solar energy fed into the grid, with midday output topping 40,000 MW.
body:
Germany fed 12 billion kilowatt-hours of solar power into its grid during July 2026—the first month in history to cross that threshold. The achievement underscores the nation's accelerating shift toward renewable energy.

The milestone carries particular weight in context: at midday, solar panels generated more than 40,000 megawatts of power—a figure that surpasses the output of Germany's entire nuclear fleet. This single statistic reveals how thoroughly solar capacity has transformed the country's energy landscape in recent years.

The record reflects both expanding solar infrastructure and favorable summer conditions, yet it points to a larger trend. As Germany continues retiring its nuclear plants, renewable sources like solar are stepping in to meet demand, proving that alternatives can deliver real power at scale.

Midday peak output reached more than 40,000 MW
Solar output exceeded all German nuclear capacity combined
